lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.29 - A Listen and read

details: Listen and read consolidates the unit's language within a narrative context. Students read and listen to understand the plot, follow the dialogue, and comprehend the story's humorous conclusion, as well as learn new vocabulary.
Look for students actively following the text, showing understanding of the dialogue through their reactions, and laughing or smiling at the final picture and punchline.

“Do you want to go to a buffet? What do you want to eat? Let’s get some ideas! Nick and Rosa went to a buffet at the weekend, but I think Nick was much hungrier than Rosa! Let's read to find out what happened.”

Heads Up (Reading): 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and help Ss to understand the text by asking questions, practicing skimming (reading for gist), scanning (reading for specific information) and detail (reading for comprehension). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down (Listen and Follow): 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together (Video, then act it out): 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.29 - B. Choose or write the correct answers.

details: Choose or write the correct answers checks students' comprehension of the story. The mixed-format questions require them to recall key details about what the characters ate and how the food tasted.
Look for the correct picture choice for question 1, the correct adjective choice for question 2, and the correctly written word ("everything") for question 3.
“That was a funny story! But I can’t remember everything that happened. Who had the tuna? Did Nick have fruit salad? Let’s see if you can help me!”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

Homework Check:
Have Ss open to the previous lesson’s homework. Score completion %. Conduct activity feedback and error correction. Score achievement %. 
Project Gallery:
Check and encourage Ss to complete the project prompts so that they are ready to present by lesson 7,

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.85 - A Read and number.

details: Read and number checks students' understanding of narrative structure and sequencing. Students must read the jumbled parts of the story and number them in the correct chronological order.
Look for the correct sequence of numbers (1-4) written in the boxes, demonstrating that students have understood the logical flow of the story.
“Oh no… we’ve got some parts of the story here but they are in the wrong order! Who did that? Let’s see how fast we can fix them! ”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.85 - B Read and circle T (True) or F (False).

details: Read and circle T or F assesses reading for specific detail. Students must read each statement carefully and decide if it is true or false based on the information given in the story.
Look for accurately circled answers (T or F) for all four statements, showing a clear comprehension of the story's key facts.
“Thank you for fixing the story! Now, I've written down some facts about it, but I'm not sure if they are all correct. Could you be a fact-checker and circle True or False for me?”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.85 - C Unscramble and match.

details: Unscramble and match consolidates the spelling and meaning of the new vocabulary from the reading. Students unscramble the letters, write the words, and then match them to the correct pictures.
Look for the correctly spelled words and accurately drawn lines connecting each word to its corresponding picture.
“Someone has really made a mess of all the words here. I can’t read them at all! What do they say? Maybe the pictures will help you…”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

Homework Set:
Complete an example of the homework to check Ss understanding. Have Ss then write the homework page, activity and plan in their diaries. 
Leaderboard:
Show the Leaderboard and congratulate / encourage daily app practise.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.30 - C Imagine you went to a buffet for lunch. Write and share.

details: Write and share provides a free-production task for the unit. Students use the prompts to write about their own imagined buffet experience, then share their ideas with a partner.
Look for logically completed written answers that use the target language, and listen for confident sharing and interaction between partners.

“We've read about what Nick and Rosa had at the buffet. Now it's your turn! Imagine you went to a buffet yesterday. Please answer the questions to write about your own experience, and then share it with a friend.”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.30 - D. Make Your Own Story Presentation

details: The Presentation serves as a culminating, productive task for the unit. Students first use a template to write a personalized dialogue, then present their story to the class to demonstrate fluency and command of the language.
Look for a logically completed written dialogue that uses the target language correctly, and a clear, confident, and audible presentation delivered to the class.

“Do you want to be the star of the story? I do! Let’s use this template to write about our own buffet experience. What did you eat? Was it delicious? How did it taste? I want to hear your amazing stories!”
